Item 1A. Risk Factors
The following risk factors could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. You should carefully consider all of the risks described below before making an investment decision. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently deem immaterial, may also impair our business operations. The order in which the risks are presented is not intended to reflect our expectation of their relative magnitude or any priority as to their likelihood of occurring.
Our revenue is concentrated among a small number of customers, and the loss of any of them would harm our operating results.
A significant portion of our revenue is derived from a few large customers. If we lose one of these customers, or if such a customer reduces its purchases, our operating results would be materially and adversely affected. This concentration also exposes us to bargaining pressure on pricing and to payment risk over time. Our contracts with these customers are generally terminable on short notice and do not guarantee any minimum purchase volume, so a change in a single relationship can have an outsized effect on a given period. We may be unable to replace lost revenue on comparable terms, or at all.
We have a history of operating losses and may never achieve or sustain profitability.
We have incurred operating losses in each fiscal year since our inception and expect to continue to invest heavily in our operations. We may never achieve or sustain profitability, and our accumulated deficit may continue to grow for the foreseeable future as we pursue our growth strategy. Achieving profitability will depend on our ability to grow revenue faster than our costs, which we may be unable to do given competitive, macroeconomic, and execution risks that are outside of our control and difficult to forecast with any precision.
Substantial doubt may exist about our ability to continue as a going concern.
Our recurring losses from operations and negative cash flows raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern within one year after the date these financial statements are issued. If we are unable to raise additional capital on acceptable terms, we may be forced to curtail or cease our operations. Any such financing may be dilutive to existing stockholders or contain restrictive covenants, and the perception that we may be unable to continue as a going concern may itself impair our ability to raise capital, retain customers and employees, and operate our business in the ordinary course.
